title: Cancer: current or history, and metastases
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's cancer as documented at this visit.
note:
Chief Complaint: Bone pain.

HPI: (Copied Forward) Patient is an 83-year-old male with a history of prostate cancer. The primary cancer was surgically removed and treated several years ago. Treatment is complete, and there is no evidence of local recurrence at the primary site.
(Update) Today, the patient presents with increasing discomfort in his lower back and hips. He reports that the pain has become more persistent over the last month. He notes that while the original site remains stable, he is experiencing new localized aching in the skeletal system.

Medication List:
- Lisinopril 10mg daily
- Atorvastatin 20mg daily
- Alendronate 70mg weekly

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 74, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 98.6F.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative for fever or chills.
Musculoskeletal: Positive for back and hip pain.
Neurological: Negative for numbness or weakness.
All other systems reviewed and are negative.

Exam:
General: Well-appearing, in no acute distress.
Musculoskeletal: Tenderness noted over the lumbar spine and bilateral hips. No visible deformity.
Skin: No lesions or rashes.

Assessment:
1. Bone metastasis from prostate carcinoma. The patient has established metastatic to bone disease which requires management of pain and skeletal integrity.

Plan:
1. Initiate scheduled imaging to evaluate the extent of the bone metastasis.
2. Start scheduled analgesics for pain management.
3. Follow up in four weeks to monitor progress.

Electronically signed, M. Okafor, MD, 05/14/2026
explanations: The prostate cancer was excised or eradicated, no treatment is directed to it and there is no evidence of it: personal history Z85.46 (no HCC). Any metastasis is still coded as a current secondary malignancy.
Bone metastases: C79.51, secondary malignant neoplasm of bone (HCC 18, which outranks the primary-site HCC).

distractors.why: Treatment ended and there is no evidence of the primary: code personal history (Z85), not active cancer.
Metastasis is coded as a secondary malignancy, even when the primary is history.
The metastases are in bone, not the liver.

hccs.label: Cancer Metastatic to Bone/Other and Unspecified Metastatic Cancer; Acute Leukemia Except Myeloid
